statement.text:
As in 17.57, let r(m) = {r + km | k ∈ Z} for integers 0 ⩽ r < m; for
r1 (m1 ) ∩ r2 (m2 ) = ∅ let the class transposition τr1 (m1 ),r2 (m2 ) be the involution which
interchanges r1 + tm1 and r2 + tm2 for each integer t and fixes everything else, and
let CT(Z) be the group generated by all class transpositions.
    Let CTk be the subgroup of CT(Z) generated by the class transpositions τr1 (k),r2 (k)
for 0 ⩽ r1 ̸= r2 < k. Since τr1 (k),r2 (k) permutes the residue classes modulo k, the group
CTk is isomorphic to the symmetric group Sk . Let CT(k) = ⟨CT2 , CT3 , . . . , CTk ⟩.
Is it true that for k > 3 the group CT(k) is isomorphic to the symmetric group SN ,
where N is the least common multiple of the numbers 2, 3, . . . , k?
                                                                V. G. Bardakov, A. L. Iskra
  ∗ Yes, it is true (Junyao Pan, Preprint of 14 April 2026, https:
//arxiv.org/abs/2604.12553;    P. Monticone, Preprint of 30 April 2026,
https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/
05/21_8-1.pdf).
